question: In an Apple Software Engineer (IS&T Backend) loop, one of the technical rounds asked the candidate to **create an immutable class in Java, with full working code expected.**
lookingFor: Knowing the rules that make a class truly immutable.
Spotting the mutable-field and leaking-reference pitfalls.
Understanding why immutability matters (thread safety, hashing, caching).
followUps: Why is String immutable in Java?
How would a record differ from this class?
What is the difference between `final` reference and immutable object?
How does immutability help in multithreaded code?
